user_stories.story: As the owner, I see a "tests" workflow in the repo's GitHub Actions tab that runs the pytest suite on every push and pull request to main, so I learn about breakage without running tests by hand.
As the owner, CI runs the suite against a throwaway PostgreSQL service whose database name ends in _test, so it behaves like my local README test setup.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Exactly one new file, `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (repo root), is added. It is valid YAML and a valid GitHub Actions workflow (top-level `name`, `on`, `jobs`). No other file is created or modified except requirements.txt (amendment 1). No README change, no Dockerfile/compose use.
`on` contains `push` and `pull_request`, each restricted to branch `main` (`branches: [main]`). No schedule, no manual dispatch required.

A single job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, sets up Python 3.12 (`actions/setup-python`, `python-version: "3.12"`). Pip caching (`cache: pip`) is optional; if used it must key off `requirements.txt` and not break the job.

The job declares a `postgres` service container with: a pinned major-version image (`postgres:17` or `postgres:16`; not `latest`); env `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_DB` where `POSTGRES_DB` ends in `_test` (e.g. `dailylog_test`); port mapping `5432:5432`; and a health check (`--health-cmd pg_isready` with `--health-interval`, `--health-timeout`, `--health-retries` options) so steps start only once the database accepts connections.

The test step (or job) sets `TEST_DATABASE_URL` to a `postgresql://:@localhost:5432/` URL whose user, password and database name match the service env and whose database name ends in `_test`. The password is a throwaway CI-only value written in the file (no repository secrets needed). `DATABASE_URL` is not set anywhere in the workflow (in particular never equal to `TEST_DATABASE_URL`), since conftest refuses that.

Steps in order: checkout (`actions/checkout`), setup Python, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, run tests. The test step uses working directory `backend` and the command `python -m pytest -q tests`, matching the README "Test" section.

Since GitHub cannot be run, verification is local: (a) the file parses with a YAML loader (e.g. PyYAML `safe_load`) and the parsed structure satisfies criteria 1-6 (triggers, image tag, health options, ports, `_test` db name, env, working directory, command, absence of `DATABASE_URL`); (b) if a PostgreSQL is reachable, the same steps are reproduced locally from a clean venv: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then in `backend`, with TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a database named `*_test` and DATABASE_URL unset, `python -m pytest -q tests` passes. If no Postgres is reachable, (b) is reported as not run. Verification never connects to the user's real `dailylog` database, never touches `uploads/` or `logs.db`, and never starts or uses anything on port 8000; any temporary Postgres or server uses another port and is stopped afterward.

requirements.txt line `psycopg[binary]==3.2` (uninstallable: needs psycopg-binary==3.2.0.dev1) becomes `psycopg[binary]==3.3.6`, matching the user's working .venv. No other requirements line changes. A fresh Python 3.12 venv installs requirements.txt without error.

out_of_scope.item: Lint/format/type-check jobs, coverage, matrix of Python versions or OSes, artifacts, deployment.
Docker/compose, README changes, requirements changes beyond criterion 8, branch protection settings.
Committing or pushing the file (the user decides).

assumptions.assumption: Postgres 17 is an acceptable pinned major version (local dev runs 18, which is not needed in CI).
Python 3.12 only; README states 3.10+ but the request fixes 3.12.
A hard-coded throwaway password in the workflow is fine because the service is ephemeral and only reachable inside the runner.

edge_cases.case: Service not yet ready when tests start: health check must gate the job.
Runner has no `.env` or DATABASE_URL: tests must still pass since they read only TEST_DATABASE_URL.
The suite's real-uploads guard reads the project-root `uploads/`, which may not exist in a fresh checkout; it must not fail (existing code tolerates a missing folder).

risks.risk: Workflow behavior on GitHub cannot be executed here, so a typo in Actions-specific keys passes YAML parsing but fails remotely; mitigated by checking structure against the criteria.
Pinned requirements.txt could include a package without wheels for Python 3.12 on Linux; reproducing the install locally reduces this.

dependencies.dependency: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner, actions/checkout, actions/setup-python, postgres Docker image.
Existing files read only: backend/tests/conftest.py, requirements.txt, README.md Test section.

spec.self_critique: Both stories map to criteria (1-3, 6 for the workflow; 4-5 for Postgres). Each criterion is checkable by parsing the YAML. The biggest unknown is real-GitHub behavior, which only a first remote run can confirm; no blocking ambiguity remains, so no clarifications.
